## Appearance

Anne is characterized by a thin figure, a pointed freckled face, and solemn gray eyes that can dilate until they appear almost black. Her features are delicate, featuring a slim milk-white throat and a bright face with big, starry eyes. Her hair is notably red, worn at times as long red braids or as short, silky curls, though people eventually describe it as auburn or ruddy. At one point, a dye attempt leaves her hair a dull, bronzy green mixed with streaks of her original red.

## Personality

Anne is a bright, diligent, and smart youth who possesses a extraordinarily vivid imagination and a dramatic flair, though she can be heedless, impulsive, forgetful, and quick-tempered with an unpraiseworthy tenacity for holding grudges. Although once considered featherbrained, she develops into a steady and reliable person who actively strives to overcome her tendency to talk too much. academically ambitious, she aims to pass high for the sake of [Matthew](../character/matthew-cuthbert.md) and [Marilla](../character/marilla-cuthbert.md), works hard to win the Avery scholarship, and intends to attend [Redmond College](../codex/places.md#redmond-college) in September while hoping to grow up to be like Mrs. [Allan](../character/allan.md). Her skills include reading and memorizing poetry, reciting dramatic pieces in public, rowing a flat-bottomed dory, and treating croup in children due to past experience. Additionally, she possesses a good singing voice, though her lively fancy can lead her to fear the [Haunted Wood](../codex/places.md#haunted-wood) after dark.

## History

Orphaned when she was just three months old, Anne Shirley spent her early years living with Mrs. [Thomas](../character/thomas-lynde.md), working for Mrs. [Hammond](../character/hammond.md), and residing in an asylum at [Hopeton](../codex/places.md#hopeton). She was brought to [Green Gables](../codex/places.md#green-gables), where [Marilla](../character/marilla-cuthbert.md) and [Matthew Cuthbert](../character/matthew-cuthbert.md) ultimately decided to adopt her despite initially expecting a boy. Early in her time there, Anne formed a deep friendship with [Diana Barry](../character/diana-barry.md) after swearing a solemn oath, though their bond was temporarily strained when Anne accidentally got [Diana](../character/diana-barry.md) drunk on currant wine. After saving Diana's young sister [Minnie May](../character/minnie-may.md) from croup, Anne won back the approval of Diana's mother. Her school life was marked by a fierce academic rivalry and feud with [Gilbert Blythe](../character/gilbert-blythe.md), whom she rejected after he pulled her hair and insulted her looks. Despite numerous misadventures—including accidentally serving liniment cake to the minister's wife and breaking her ankle in a dare—Anne excelled academically under Miss Stacy's guidance. She won the prestigious Avery scholarship upon graduating from Queen's [Academy](../codex/places.md#academy), bringing great pride to [Matthew](../character/matthew-cuthbert.md) just before his sudden death from heart failure caused by news of a bank collapse. To save [Green Gables](../codex/places.md#green-gables) and care for the sight-impaired [Marilla](../character/marilla-cuthbert.md), Anne chose to give up her college scholarship to teach locally. Her long-standing feud with [Gilbert](../character/gilbert-blythe.md) ended when he selflessly gave up his [Avonlea](../codex/places.md#avonlea) teaching position for her, allowing them to finally become close friends.

## Quotes

> "You can punish me in any way you like, Marilla. You can shut me up in a dark, damp dungeon inhabited by snakes and toads and feed me only on bread and water and I shall not complain. But I cannot ask Mrs. Lynde to forgive me."
>
> — Anne Shirley — [v1 CHAPTER IX. Mrs. Rachel Lynde Is Properly Horrified P46](../source/v01-c09.md#nw-v01-c09-p0046)

> "Pretty well. I imagine a good deal, and that helps to pass the time. Of course, it’s rather lonesome. But then, I may as well get used to that."
>
> — Anne Shirley — [v1 CHAPTER X. Anne’s Apology P11](../source/v01-c10.md#nw-v01-c10-p0011)

> "I don’t get cross about other things; but I’m so tired of being twitted about my hair and it just makes me boil right over. Do you suppose my hair will really be a handsome auburn when I grow up?"
>
> — Anne Shirley — [v1 CHAPTER X. Anne’s Apology P43](../source/v01-c10.md#nw-v01-c10-p0043)

> "I love pretty things; and I hate to look in the glass and see something that isn’t pretty. It makes me feel so sorrowful—just as I feel when I look at any ugly thing. I pity it because it isn’t beautiful."
>
> — Anne Shirley — [v1 CHAPTER X. Anne’s Apology P45](../source/v01-c10.md#nw-v01-c10-p0045)

> "I love Green Gables already, and I never loved any place before. No place ever seemed like home. Oh, Marilla, I’m so happy. I could pray right now and not find it a bit hard."
>
> — Anne Shirley — [v1 CHAPTER X. Anne’s Apology P49](../source/v01-c10.md#nw-v01-c10-p0049)

## Relationships

### [Allan](../character/allan.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/allan--anne-shirley.md)

Mrs. [Allan](../character/allan.md) is the local minister's wife who quickly becomes a trusted confidante to Anne. Despite an embarrassing initial blunder where Anne accidentally serves her a cake flavored with liniment, Mrs. [Allan](../character/allan.md) responds with kindness and comfort. Anne frequently visits her to share joyful news, such as her entrance exam results, and seeks her counsel when dealing with deep personal sorrow.

### [Diana Barry](../character/diana-barry.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/anne-shirley--diana-barry.md)

[Diana Barry](../character/diana-barry.md) is Anne's closest friend and soulmate, having sworn a solemn oath of friendship shortly after meeting. Their bond faces a severe test when Diana's mother forbids them from playing together, but they are reunited after Anne saves the life of Diana's sick younger sister through a night of careful nursing. The two act as constant confidantes and share in school activities and childhood play.

### [Gilbert Blythe](../character/gilbert-blythe.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/anne-shirley--gilbert-blythe.md)

Anne and [Gilbert](../character/gilbert-blythe.md) share a complex, tense relationship that begins when [Gilbert](../character/gilbert-blythe.md) mockingly calls her "Carrots," prompting Anne to smash a slate over his head and refuse his attempts to apologize. Though [Gilbert](../character/gilbert-blythe.md) rescues her from a sinking boat in a dory, Anne coldly rejects his olive branch, cementing an intense academic rivalry at school. Despite keeping her distance and maintaining her grudge, Anne secretly regrets the ongoing feud and misses his attention.

### [Josephine Barry](../character/josephine-barry.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/anne-shirley--josephine-barry.md)

[Aunt Josephine](../character/josephine-barry.md) [Barry](../character/josephine-barry.md) initially reacts with fury when Anne accidentally leaps onto her in bed during a sleepover. ### [Marilla Cuthbert](../character/marilla-cuthbert.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/anne-shirley--marilla-cuthbert.md)

[Marilla Cuthbert](../character/marilla-cuthbert.md) is Anne's adoptive mother figure who initially intended to return the young orphan due to a mix-up over wanting a boy. After hearing Anne's tragic background and seeing her need for a good home, [Marilla](../character/marilla-cuthbert.md) decides to keep her and takes charge of her moral and practical upbringing. Though [Marilla](../character/marilla-cuthbert.md) frequently scolds Anne's theatrical nature, the two develop a deep, reciprocal love.
